headline: Tarique Rahman to address UN General Assembly for the first time
summary: The Prime Minister will travel to New York for the 81st session of the UNGA, becoming the third member of his family to speak at the forum.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is set to make his first address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Thursday. He will travel to New York for the 81st session of the assembly, where he will outline Bangladesh's vision for the future and its national priorities.

Tarique Rahman becomes the third member of his family to address the UNGA. His father, late president Ziaur Rahman, spoke on August 26, 1980, and his mother, late prime minister Khaleda Zia, addressed the assembly on five separate occasions between 1993 and 2005.

The Prime Minister's visit includes a packed schedule of over a dozen bilateral meetings. He is expected to meet with leaders from Canada, Thailand, Bhutan, Pakistan, Kuwait, Croatia, and Saudi Arabia, as well as officials from the World Bank and the UN Secretary-General.

A major priority of the visit is the Rohingya crisis, with Bangladesh planning a high-level side event to discuss the issue. The government aims to use the forum to present Bangladesh as a democratic, confident, and responsible country.
The 81st session of the General Assembly is currently being presided over by Bangladeshi Foreign Minister Dr. Khalilur Rahman, who was elected President of the assembly in June.

headline: 13-year-old Opratim's body recovered 24 hours after going missing in Cumilla
summary: The only son of a Comilla University professor, 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, was found dead yesterday after being missing for nearly a day. His janaza was held today.
details: The first namaz-e-janaza of 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim was held at the playground beside the Central Jame Mosque of Comilla University at 10:13am today. The university's vice-chancellor, along with teachers, officials, employees and students, attended the janaza.

Opratim's body was recovered yesterday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after he went missing from the Kotbari-Gandhamati area of Cumilla city. He was a class-VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School.

He was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor in the Bangla Department at Comilla University, and KM Firoz Shahriar, a businessman. The second janaza will be held at the Gandhamati Eidgah ground at 11:00am, after which Opratim will be buried at the Kotbari-Gandhamati graveyard.

Opratim's body was recovered yesterday afternoon, nearly 24 hours after he went missing from the Kotbari-Gandhamati area of Cumilla city. He was a class-VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School.
